 The Honourable Sri Justice J.Sreenivas Rao

 Date: 30.03.2026

 And

Hyderabad and six others.

entities.text:
High Court For The State Of Telangana
 At Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This Writ Petition is filed seeking to quashquestioning the action of the respondent No.4 seeking to quash the proceedings in F.I.R.No.776 of 2023 and in completing the investigation by the Investigating Officer and forwarding final report on 26.06.2025 on the file of X Additional Metropolitan Magistrate, Cyberabad at Kukatpally and other reliefs.

2. Heard Mr. Rajesh Maddy, learned counsel for the petitioners, and Mr. B. Sreedhar, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home appearing on behalf of respondent Nos.1 to 4.
3.

During the course of the hearing, the learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home, based on the information available on the E-Courts website, submitted that even prior to the filing of the writ petition, the learned Magistrate had taken cognizance based on the final report filed by the Investigating Officer for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420, 467, 468, and 471 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, and the same has been numbered as C.C.No.2089 of 2025.

He further submitted that, insofar as the other relief sought by the petitioner with respect to setting aside the Look-out circular issued against the petitioner is concerned, the same has been deleted by the Investigating Officer.

4. He further submitted that by virtue of the principle laid down by the Apex Court in Pradnya Pranjal Kulkarni v. State of Maharashtra 1, the writ petition filed by the petitioner, seeking to quash C.C. No. 94 of 2018 invoking the jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, is not maintainable in law, as the learned Magistrate has taken cognizance.

entities.text: Pradnya Pranjal Kulkarni v. State of Maharashtra 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
5. Taking into consideration the above submissions as well as the principle laid down by the Hon'ble G.Vijaya Bhaskar vs The State Of Telangana on 30 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116817354/
1

entities.text: G.Vijaya Bhaskar vs The State Of Telangana on 30 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Apex Court in Pradnya Pranjal SLA (CRL) No.13424 of 2025, dt. 03.09.2025 Kulkarni's case (supra), this Court is of the considered view that the petitioner is not entitled to the relief sought in the writ petition.
6. Accordingly, the writ petition is closed.
However, petitioner is granted liberty to avail the remedies as available under law, if so he is aggrieved.
Pending miscellaneous applications, if any, shall stand closed.

JUSTICE J. SREENIVAS RAO 30.03.2026 ggd G.Vijaya Bhaskar vs The State Of Telangana on 30 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116817354/
